item.title: China Open Source Daily — 2026-11-28
item.description: Revolut moved roughly 2,000 engineers onto a self-hosted GLM-5.3 running on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs it bought itself, and reports a 90 per cent cut in inference cost against Claude Code and Codex — a flat bill, no per-seat token anxiety, and the vendor's future decisions removed from the dependency. This briefing reads the case as the first complete receipt for a Chinese open-weight licence, and pairs it with an artefact the same ecosystem did not build: discretionary segment figures that cannot be reconciled to any statutory line. One receipt is admissible because a buyer with a budget published it. The other is not a number at all, because where no regulator requires arithmetic, no arithmetic appears. Open weights have been China's one product in this ecosystem that a stranger can verify for himself.
